text:
Alex Morgan: Hey all 11 I'm Alex, joining cloud infra this week. Two quick setup asks as I start my first ticket: 
- Please link billing account `billing-redwood-sandbox` to project `redwood-sandbox-alex` so I can spin up test VMs in us-central1 and europe-west1.
- Grant my user roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 on the project and roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on service account `sa-alex@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
- Need AWS read-only (cross-account) to account `123456789012` and S3 ListObjects on `redwood-model-checkpoints` bucket to inspect checkpoint sizes.
- Okta MFA is set but CLI gcloud is failing with "invalid grant" when I try to use device flow. Any quick fixes?
Who should I tag for billing link + AWS cross-account? Thanks!

Nadia Ortiz: welcome Alex! For billing link ping @billing-team, but I can start the link if you add me to the project iam policy. We usually want a short justification in the ticket (one-liner).

Alex Morgan: Added justification: "Sandbox experiments for dev infra ramp; non-prod spend under $50/mo expected."

Tom Reyes: tagging security. A couple things: if the project touches external accounts we require least privilege and time-limited AWS role bindings (default 72h). Also do not upload service account keys to Git. Use iam-bot to create short-lived creds if needed.

Claire Wu: Re: gcloud CLI error 1 I had that yesterday. Try `gcloud auth application-default login --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` and then `gcloud auth login` in a separate shell. If it still fails, check Okta Device flow app is enabled for your account.

Alex Morgan: Thanks Claire 1 I tried those commands and got past the device flow error after re-enrolling in Okta MFA.

iam-bot: Noted. To grant roles I need the target principal. Alex, do you want the roles on the project for your user email `alex.morgan@redwood.com` or on the service account to be assumed by CI?

Alex Morgan: Grant compute.instanceAdmin.v1 to my user `alex.morgan@redwood.com` and serviceAccountUser on `sa-alex@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for the CI pipeline. Time-limited AWS read-only for 72h is fine.

Nadia Ortiz: I submitted a billing link request - ticket BILL-1043. Please confirm you see the project under "Billing" in console.

ops-bot: Ticket OPS-4902 created by Nadia Ortiz. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4902

iam-bot: Applied `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` to `alex.morgan@redwood.com` at 1905123500. Applied `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` to CI principal at 1905123525.

Tom Reyes: Security reviewed AWS request; temporary role will be created with `sts:AssumeRole` allowed for 72 hours and CloudTrail alerted. Do not copy S3 objects externally.

Alex Morgan: I can see the billing now and confirm compute role works (able to create a tiny n1-standard1 instance in us-central1). Thanks! :raised_hands: 

Nadia Ortiz: Great. Leaving this open until AWS role is active and you confirm S3 list access.

iam-bot: AWS temporary role created for `alex.morgan@redwood.com` to assume in account `123456789012`. Expiry set to 72 hours. Use `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Redwood-ReadOnly --role-session-name alex-temp`

Alex Morgan: Confirmed S3 List works. Can list bucket and preview object keys. All good on my end. Closing this thread once ops tickets are linked.

ops-bot: Updated OPS-4902 with BILL-1043 linkage and AWS request reference.
